newsitem.title: UK: Dlr struggles in Europe, some bulls bailing out.
newsitem.headline: Dlr struggles in Europe, some bulls bailing out.

text.p: The dollar continued to struggle in European trade as dealers bailed out of long positions whenever the currency made new ground, traders said on Thursday.

After a three-pfennig slide on Wednesday, the dollar started to recover only to run into resistance. A potentially bearish chart pattern and German interest rate speculation were seen as the main barriers.
"There are still a few stale dollar longs," said a trader at a European bank in London. "If it does get back up, I'd expect to see the sellers come back in around 1.85 (marks)."
Traders also said the dollar will be at the mercy of U.S. stocks and bonds, which are waiting for consumer price (CPI) data at 1230 GMT and industrial production and capacity utilisation at 1315 GMT.
At 1115 GMT, the dollar was at 1.8340/50 marks, not far from 1.8355/60 late here on Wednesday. It had pushed up to 1.84440 earlier in the session.
Dollar/yen was at 116.51/56, up from 115.65/75 late on Wednesday.
Overall and core U.S. July CPI are each expected to rise 0.2 percent.
U.S. July industrial production was expected to gain 0.2 percent, and capacity utilisation was remain flat at 83.5 percent.
But traders expected the U.S. data to have little impact on markets.
"There's less importance on today's numbers after yesterday's numbers because the PPI (producer price index) was benign," a trader at a European bank said.
Analysts said the mark was firmer amid rising speculation short-term German interest rates may rise.

"Residual position adjustment could continue through the rest of this week and as such, the risk is that the mark continues to recover," said Paul Meggyesi, senior analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The dollar has fallen sharply since touching a high of 1.8913 marks last week. On Wednesday, it tumbled as low as 1.8280 marks.

The dollar's ability to hold recent lows will be crucial. Failure to hold support near 1.8265-75 marks could confirm a potential "head and shoulders" pattern and send the U.S. currency lower, chart watchers said.

The mark rose across the board on Wednesday, reaching its highest level against the dollar in almost two weeks, after the Bundesbank said German inflation had picked up and that it would steer policy to ensure price stability was maintained.
The Bundesbank's comments were seen as a sign the central bank might raise interest rates.
In Asia, the Indonesian rupiah slid to a record low versus the dollar at 2,815 after Indonesia's central bank abolished its intervention band.
At midday Europe, the rupiah was straddling the record low, quoted at 2805/2835 per dollar by New York dealers.
